model: load ledger v2 (Q166, calc-a): the joined load model revived by its retirement note's recipe
form: J_total = P_idle(card, T0) t + k_leak(card, T0) dT t + J_over_idle; J_over_idle = sum_ops (Z_f + D_kind)/R_f v2 + sum_class cycles r_issue e_class v2 + awake_cycles e_awake v2 + sum_paths bytes (z + (r - z) phi) + mesh bytes hops p_hop; phi = w_set rho/0.5 + (1 - w_set) tau/0.5; dT = k_rise P_over_idle; v2 = (V/V600)^2. See tools/ledger/ledger_v2.py.

w_set.source: docs/reports/data/2026-11-01-e101-real-matmul/README.md R5 and R5b (the benchmark arm): a constant costs the path +2.09 / +1.74 / +2.43 W over zeros against random's +6.78 / +6.33 / +11.66 W (fp32 / fp16 / int8); the constants carry 7/32, 4/16 and 1/8 set bits and change none, so w_set = (ratio) / (rho / 0.5) = 0.703 / 0.550 / 0.834

awake_rule: a hart's time is priced once. The catalogue's per-byte and per-op prices were measured with their issuing harts awake for the whole transfer (e_i = (P - P_idle) / rate), so a hart's cycles blocked on its own tensor op or its own loads and stores are inside those prices up to the probe's own time per byte; its instruction-bound cycles (an epilogue, a tile's set-up, a generator's work beyond its stores) are priced as issue; only the rest of a running hart's time, waiting on another hart or the host, is priced as awake
